cells.title: Refuse a repeat dissent after a verdict unless it brings new evidence
cells.action: Per D3 (store b2baf5e0): in dissent.rs, `pub(crate) fn record_dissent(` (the one dissent writer; also called from herding/run.rs `match crate::verbs::cells::record_dissent(` — do NOT edit run.rs) keeps its exact signature and delegates to a new sibling that also takes `new_evidence: Option<&str>`. Before the cells lock is taken (the existing refusal order comment: every refusal happens BEFORE mutate_cell), the sibling reads the cell's existing dissent entries; when any entry carries a non-empty `verdict` (DISSENT_VERDICT_KEY) and `new_evidence` is absent or blank, refuse with a message that quotes the newest answered verdict and its reason and names the fix `--new-evidence "<what is new>"`; the cell file stays byte-identical. With evidence, scan it with the same `assert_safe_decision_fields` call, and store it on the new appended entry as `new_evidence`. Entries still append, never overwrite. Wire a `--new-evidence` flag on `bee cells dissent` (the run_dissent handler in dissent.rs), add the flag to the catalog.rs flag table where `--alternative` is registered, and declare it in generated/registry_payload.json for the `cells dissent` verb by hand (the same both-directions rule recorded in verbs/cells/util.rs beside `"dissent" => run_dissent`). Add the dissent-once rule, the refusal and the flag to the dissent knowledge concept. No code comments.

truths: A first dissent on a cell records as before
A dissent on a cell whose dissent already has a verdict is refused unless --new-evidence is given, and the cell file is byte-identical after the refusal
A dissent with --new-evidence after a verdict appends an entry carrying new_evidence

Validate them where `baseline` is validated (`match map.get("baseline")`): `reaction` is a string matched case-insensitively against confirm|partial|challenge|blocked and stored lowercase, else refuse quoting the allowed set; `skipped`, `unknowns`, `found` are arrays of non-empty strings (`[]` is legal and means none); `stopped` is a non-empty string; `reaction` partial without `stopped` is refused with the fix `add "stopped": "<the part not done> — <evidence>"`. Tests in cells/tests.rs: new keys stored; old report unchanged; bad reaction refused; partial without stopped refused; mixed-case reaction stored lowercase. No code comments.

A report without the new keys caps exactly as before
reaction outside the closed set, and partial without stopped, are refused by name

cells.title: Carry the new result fields, dissent evidence and the model mismatch on herding runs, with an opt-in refuse
cells.action: Three parts, one envelope. (1) Per D1 and D2: add optional `reaction`, `skipped`, `unknowns`, `found`, `stopped` to `pub(crate) struct MailboxResult` in mailbox.rs, parsed leniently exactly like `let leaning = obj.get("leaning")...` (absent or wrong-typed reads as absent, never Malformed; reaction lowercased and kept only when in confirm|partial|challenge|blocked). Name them in the result schema block of `pub(crate) fn render_brief(` as optional, in ONE short block, without naming any bee command (the existing brief pins forbid `bee ` in the brief). In run.rs `fn result_envelope(` re-emit each only when present, like `m.insert("leaning".into(), ...)`; when reaction is partial and stopped is absent, emit `stopped_missing: true`. (2) Per D3: add optional `new_evidence` to `MailboxDissent` and pass it from the transcription site `match crate::verbs::cells::record_dissent(` to rig-1's evidence-taking sibling; a refused transcription keeps `dissent_recorded: false` plus `dissent_error`. (3) Per D9 (store 0ccaa387) and the plan's settled list: add a config reader in paseo.rs for `herding.paseo.on_model_mismatch` (`warn` default when absent or unknown, `refuse`) in the style of `fn configured_command(`. Make `fn record_observed_model(` return whether a confirmed mismatch was seen. At the two in-loop call sites (inside the poll closures) with `refuse`, stop the agent with `paseo::stop_argv` through the same cli call `herding interrupt` uses in job_verbs.rs, and end the run with a typed outcome reason `model_mismatch` whose message names configured and observed model and thinking and two fixes (point the agent's paseo block at the model that runs, or set herding.paseo.on_model_mismatch to warn); exit non-zero. At the post-loop call site never refuse: keep the result and warn. In both modes the envelope carries `model_mismatch: {configured, observed}` read from the job record's paseo_model_observed / paseo_thinking_observed when paseo_model_mismatch is true. Update the two knowledge concepts: the new result fields and envelope keys in the run-verb concept, the refuse mode in the paseo-channel concept (state that today's flash route reports thinking off and would be refused). No code comments.

Wrong-typed new fields never make a result Malformed
With on_model_mismatch absent a mismatch only warns and the envelope carries model_mismatch
With refuse a mismatch seen while polling stops the agent and ends the run with reason model_mismatch
A herding dissent with new_evidence after a verdict is recorded with that evidence

cells.title: Report a write worker whose worktree stopped changing as stalled, once
cells.action: Per D7 (store 8a826f2f) and the plan's settled list. Add a reader `stall_after_secs` for `herding.stall_after_secs` (default 900) in the style of `pub(crate) fn ceiling_seconds(cfg: &Value) -> Option<u64> {`. Stall is derived in two places in herding.rs, both at `mailbox::transition_status(bee_dir, ..., "stalled")` (in compute_job_status and in the status-list loop); add ONE shared helper used by both. For a job whose job record `read_only` is not true and whose status would otherwise be working: compute a fingerprint in the job record's `cwd` = `git rev-parse HEAD` plus a hash of `git diff HEAD` stdout; store `diff_fingerprint` and `diff_fingerprint_since` on the job record when the fingerprint changes; when it is unchanged for longer than stall_after_secs, the status is `stalled` and `stall_reason` is `no_diff_progress` (the existing activity stall writes `stall_reason: activity`). A change of reason is a new stretch. On the transition into a no_diff_progress stretch, append ONE message to the job's messages file with `crate::herding::notify::append_message` (kind `progress`, text `bee: stalled — no_diff_progress for <N>s; observe only, nothing was stopped; check with bee herding status`). Nothing is stopped or retried. `recovered` fires when the fingerprint moves. A git failure in cwd leaves status unchanged. Document the signal, the knob and the read-time nature (computed when status is read) in the herding overview concept. Tests: frozen past window stalls with the reason; moving fingerprint never stalls; read-only job never stalls by fingerprint; second read appends no second message; recovery. No code comments.

truths: A write job with a frozen worktree past the window reads stalled with stall_reason no_diff_progress
A read-only job never stalls by fingerprint
Exactly one message is appended per stalled stretch

the notice goes through append_message

No edit to notify.rs or run.rs
